title: Spring Data JPA Repositories

richText: JPA maps entities to relational tables. Hibernate implements the JPA operations in a typical Spring Boot JPA application.
Spring Data JPA adds repository interfaces on top of JPA. A repository provides methods for storing and retrieving entities.
Spring creates an implementation of a declared repository interface. Application code injects that repository as a bean.
MongoRepository is a separate Spring Data MongoDB interface. It does not use JPA or Hibernate to store MongoDB documents.
CrudRepository provides create, read, update and delete methods such as save, findById and deleteById.
JpaRepository includes these operations and adds JPA-specific operations such as flush and batch deletion. It also supports paging and sorting.
The first type argument is the entity class. The second is its ID type.
Keep business rules in the service. Use the repository for persistence operations.

richText: save stores a new entity or merges an existing entity according to JPA entity-state rules. Use the returned entity.
findById returns Optional because the ID may not match any row.
findAll returns all matching rows. For a growing table, read a page instead of loading the entire table.
flush sends pending changes to the database. It is different from committing the transaction.
